mobbin:b3200869-6502-4670-a9f3-48efa536c.summary: From the week calendar, type a natural-language Schedule @ request, review hard conflicts versus inconveniences, Confirm, and see an Event created pop-up on the grid.
steps: Week grid: Find time, Lunch, Focus
Event created pop-up: Alex // Sam block
steal: The proposal splits 'conflicts that I can't fix' (for example outside working hours) from 'inconveniences' (for example 1 hour of Focus Time lost) before Confirm (screens 8 to 9).
A Flexible switch on the proposal card plus Refine request… sits with 'Nothing will change until explicitly confirmed' (screens 8 to 9).
Natural-language Schedule @… then Get proposal / Understanding request is the create path instead of a blank full form (screens 3 to 7).
After confirm, a pop-up says 'Event created' with View event while the block appears on the week grid (screen 10).
avoid: Heavy AI proposal UX and a personal Focus Time model are expensive versus the baseline simple event plus Excel import; do not require natural language to create a session.
mobbin:b3200869-6502-4670-a9f3-48efa536c.fit: Scheduling: steal graded conflict versus soft inconvenience while picking people and time. Map Focus Time to protected faculty or room blocks, not the full Clockwise automation stack.

mobbin:82616858-3a1c-482e-8596-71abfb55c.summary: Open Clockwise week calendar showing Day/Week toggle, Find time, a current-time line, and Lunch/Focus Time blocks across Mon to Fri.
steps: Week view: Find time, Lunch, Focus
steal: Day/Week toggle and Find time sit beside the calendar chrome (screens 1 to 2).
Lunch versus Focus Time use distinct block styles (border and weight) so protected capacity reads differently from meetings (screens 1 to 2).
avoid: Only two static week frames are shown, with no drag-to-reschedule or conflict UI; do not credit drag from this capture.
mobbin:82616858-3a1c-482e-8596-71abfb55c.fit: Scheduling: baseline calendar chrome reference (week grid, find-time button, protected blocks). Pair with the meeting-proposal flow for conflict UX.
